metadata.title: World Cup Betting Drives Prediction Market Trading Volume To $50 Billion

content.text:
Betting on the World Cup propelled trading volumes on prediction markets to $50 billion U.S. in June.
This year's FIFA World Cup has officially become the biggest sports betting event in history, driving record activity on prediction markets such as Kalshi and Polymarket.
Prediction markets enable people to bet on the outcome of real-world events, including sports contests and tournaments.

Kalshi posted $31 billion U.S. in trading volumes for June, a 70% increase from May of this year, with betting on sports accounting for 85% of the trading on its platform.
Kalshi said that World Cup betting on its platform totaled $22.42 billion U.S. in June.
Polymarket's international exchange set a monthly record of $10.8 billion U.S. in trading volume during June, while its regulated U.S. platform logged $3.5 billion U.S., double May's total.
Other prediction markets on platforms such as Robinhood Markets (NASDAQ: $HOOD) processed $2 billion U.S. in World Cup bets, according to data from Bank of America (NYSE: $BAC).
More traditional U.S. sportsbooks are projected to handle between $2.8 billion U.S. and $4.3 billion U.S. in betting over the course of the World Cup's 104 soccer matches.
Analysts had predicted that the World Cup would be a defining moment for prediction markets such as Kalshi and Polymarket.
FIFA named Kalshi its official prediction market partner part-way through the tournament, giving Kalshi branding rights, in-venue presence, and a media distribution deal with Fox Sports.
Both Kalshi and Polymarket are privately held and their stocks do not trade on a public exchange.
